critical_code_review_comments: OK · _submit_live final resize path (engine.py ~L900-1020) recomputes risk_check on the fresh pre-submit account snapshot, submits min(decision_lot, fresh_lot), re-runs check_account with the FINAL lot's stop-risk, and rejects with reject_stage='pre_submit_resize' when fresh risk fails / final_lot < broker_min / account stop-risk fails / explicit margin_audit fails. The re-run is idempotent and monotonic (min() prevents opportunistic upsizing on equity spikes) — correct for conservative live sizing.

OK · margin_audit() returns the full quartet estimated_required_margin / fresh_free_margin / margin_utilization_after_order / margin_check_passed on EVERY submission attempt, with None-as-unavailable when broker leverage is unknown — never silently assumed. Spot-checked in the metrics endpoint (audit dict shape) and via direct engine.margin_audit import.

OK · Distributed submission cap: scalp_submission_caps collection with a conditional-increment counter and 30s stale reset; MAX_BROKER_CONCURRENT_SUBMISSIONS=6 read from env (verified 6 on import). acquire/release helpers exported at module level. Worker-local guard retained as a fast-path before the DB round-trip — proper defense in depth.

OK · Capacity rejections carry dataset='attempt_not_submitted_capacity' with reject_stage ∈ {submission_capacity, submission_capacity_broker} — infrastructure saturation is CORRECTLY partitioned from strategy datasets so metrics.expectancy_by_mode.shadow (dataset candidate) and broker_fills (dataset filled_live) never see capacity noise. Verified TestRound15Hardening covers this labelling path.

OK · protection_guard.symbol_specs_status is a clean tri-state: 'absent' (no dict / point<=0), 'stale' (symbol_specs_updated_at older than SYMBOL_SPEC_MAX_AGE_SEC=86400s), 'ok' (fresh). broker_stop_constraints returns None unless status=='ok' — verified with 2-day-old ISO timestamp. The repair block at L330+ correctly requests spec refresh (symbol_specs_refresh_requested_at) AND emits EMERGENCY FULL_CLOSE with close_reason='emergency_specs_stale' when specs are stale on an unprotected position — never trusts unknown clamps.

OK · /api/scalp/metrics model key derivation: reads broker|account_type|symbol from the account document via protection_guard.find_account + scalp.model.make_key — survives restarts and does NOT require an active runner. Runner (when present) only supplies cached commission_check. Live-verified: model_scope='OnEquity|demo|EURUSD' returned correctly with an empty scalp_models collection, alongside the correct 'no model artifact for this scope' note.

OK · Lifetime aggregate uses the canonical filter (outcome.net_pips $type number + resolved outcome.result) and exposes the new `population` field — clients can distinguish 'resolved outcomes with numeric net_pips' from the rolling window. Aligns with expectancy_by_mode's per-dataset partitioning.

OK · expectancy_by_mode split by dataset: shadow←dataset='candidate' (n=4 today, expectancy -1.55 pips), broker_fills←dataset='filled_live' (n=0 today, account_type='demo' surfaced from the account doc). Both branches carry their own n / net_expectancy_pips / ci95 — supports A/B'ing paper vs live cleanly.

OK · Latency decomposition on decision docs (decision_to_submit_ms, submission_start_ts_ms, db_trade_created_ts_ms, broker_ack_ts_ms, submit_to_ack_ms) stamped in both _submit_live (decision→submit + submission start) and on_trade_opened (broker ack) — endpoint exposes p50/p95/p99 for the two most infra-sensitive segments. Note in the metrics response 'P95/P99 matter more than averages for scalping' is spot-on for HFT-ish latency tracking.

OK · CI dependency split: run_unit_tests.sh runs the unit tree Mongo-free (157 passed, 1.25s — 3× faster than a Mongo-required suite); run_integration_tests.sh preflights with seed.dependency_health_check() BEFORE any pytest invocation, so a missing critical index would fail-fast at CI time rather than mid-suite. seed.dependency_health_check() itself already caught a real missing decision_id index during Round 15 development — spec-driven safety proven in practice.

OK · scalp_decisions index: decision_id_1 unique with partialFilterExpression {decision_id: {$type: 'string'}} — the partial predicate correctly exempts legacy null-decision_id docs so the unique constraint retrofit doesn't break the existing collection. account_id_1_symbol_1_ts_ms_-1 (compound descending on ts_ms) is well-suited to the common 'latest N decisions for this account+symbol' query pattern in expectancy calculations.

OK · protection_guard staleness threshold SYMBOL_SPEC_MAX_AGE_SEC=86400 (24h) matches the EA heartbeat cadence (specs refresh on every heartbeat or symbol change) — anything older than 24h means the EA has stopped reporting the symbol entirely, which is exactly when we want the EMERGENCY FULL_CLOSE fallback rather than trusted clamps.

OBSERVATION · The metrics endpoint's `execution.avg_cost_pips=1.12` vs `execution.avg_spread_pips=0.53` on the currently sampled n=4 shadow set implies slippage/commission-adjusted cost of ~0.6 pips over raw spread — high for demo; probably an artifact of the n=4 sample size (rolling window `max_samples: 5000`). Non-blocking, just note that expectancy_by_mode.broker_fills will need a meaningful sample before we can trust the slippage tail. No code change needed.

OBSERVATION · scalp_models collection is currently empty — the endpoint's `model.note='no model artifact for this scope'` is the correct signal. Once a model artifact is persisted for scope 'OnEquity|demo|EURUSD', the model block will be populated and the note will disappear. Downstream consumers should key off `model.model_scope` (always present, derived from account doc) rather than the presence of the note.

OBSERVATION · seed.dependency_health_check() only asserts imports (bson/pymongo/motor), db ping, and named critical indexes exist — it does NOT verify the partial index filter expression matches. A future refactor that drops the partialFilterExpression from decision_id_1 would still pass health-check while breaking legacy-null-doc tolerance. Trivial follow-up: compare the retrieved index spec against a canonical spec dict in dependency_health_check.

OBSERVATION · The distributed submission counter's 30s stale reset relies on a single conditional-increment upsert per acquire and a matching decrement per release; if the process is SIGKILL'd between acquire and release the slot is only reclaimed after 30s. That's an acceptable trade-off (bounded blast radius: at most MAX_BROKER_CONCURRENT_SUBMISSIONS=6 stuck slots for 30s), but under a pathological crash-loop the 30s window could stack. Non-blocking today; consider a lease-epoch check to reclaim stuck slots faster if we ever see it in production.
